textbookText: Robert Hooke [Born on July 18 (July 28, New Style), 1635, Freshwater, Isle England], is an English physicist who discovered the law of elasticity, known as Hooke’s law. In 1655 Hooke was employed by Robert Boyle to construct the Boylean air pump. Five years later, Hooke discovered his law of elasticity, which states that the stretching of a solid body (e.g., metal wood) is proportional to the force applied to it. The law laid the basis for studies of stress and strain and for understanding of elastic materials. He applied these studies in his designs for the balance springs of watches; his interest in timekeeping was further reflected in his effort to improve the pendulum for clock regulation. Robert Hooke has (1660) developed a mathematical relationship between tension and extension. In 1660, he discovered the law of elasticity which states the stretching of a solid is proportional to the force applied. Poison, Cauchy and G Stoke showed the equation of the general theory of elasticity. In 1662 he was appointed curator of experiments to the Royal Society of London and was elected a fellow the following year.

i) Take a metallic (or a hard rubber) spring with a small marble attached at the free ends and, place it on a table. ii) Bring the marbles close to each other and then release them. Observe what happens next. iii) Pull the marbles away from each other and release them again. Observe what happens. Think for yourself and collect more ideas on what‘s going on there.

The force given in either case is the deforming force that changes the configuration of the body. When the deforming force in either case is removed, the body regains its original configuration. In doing so, there is a force setting up internally, called the restoring force. When the deforming force employed to extend the spring is large enough, the body can’t regain its original configuration. Such a stage is the stage of plasticity, and the body is said to be in a plastic stage (or in a damaged state in some context of engineering and structural analysis). When a body regains its original configuration, it is in the elastic stage, and the phenomenon is elasticity. Hence elasticity is the property of a matter by virtue of which it regains its original shape and size after the removal of the deforming force. In physics, the more the rigidity, the more is the elasticity. Hence this is why iron is said to be more elastic than rubber. In the same sense, a solid is more elastic than a liquid and the liquid is more elastic than gases. The origin of elasticity is due to the presence of short-range molecular interaction inside the matter. Every matter is made of atoms and molecules. The separation of such particles in a normal state is ro. If the material is elongated using a deforming force, the separation ro increases, and an attractive force between the particles comes into play, returning it to its original configuration. If the body is contracted, ro decreases, and a repulsive force establishes itself, capable of returning it to its original configuration. If the deforming force is so large that the distance between the particles is much greater than ro, the two particles cannot attract each other, and the body is in the plastic stage. Hence, the point of the deforming force at which the body regains its original configuration is the elastic limit. Beyond this point, the body is in the plastic stage (or damaged in the case considered).

Concept to know: i) Springs are generally made of steel rather than copper because springs are used in spring balance for which the material of the spring should have high value of elasticity. Steel is more elastic than copper, and requires greater force for the same extension. Hence, we favor steel for the spring. ii) RCC rods are used in the construction of buildings. In physics, the rods have a high degree of elasticity, allowing buildings to regain their shape even after a heavy earthquake . The design and materials used in these rods contribute to the overall resilience of the structure. iii) High-tension cable is commonly found in a twisted form.
